newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Fate of Venezuela airline to be settled this week.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Venezuela airline to be settled this week.

text.p: The future of troubled Venezuelan airline Viasa will be decided on Friday when shareholders are expected to vote on whether to declare the carrier bankrupt, company officials said on Tuesday.

Odds for the Venezuelan carrier to survive its prolonged crisis dimmed when a leading French investment bank reportedly withdrew an offer to help. Banque Paribas, contracted by workers last year to advise on potential investors for the airline, was quoted as saying it preferred to wait on the sidelines for the time being.
"Furthermore, should it be necessary, they will return again as advisers," William Bracho, president of Viasa's workers union, told reporters, citing a Paribas letter.
Officials at Banque Paribas in Caracas were not immediately available for comment.

Viasa grounded all its planes on Thursday, stranding hundreds of passengers. Its executive board originally set the extraordinary shareholders' meeting for Feb. 8, but it was brought forward to Friday "due to the grave emergency," one company source told Reuters.
The airline's decision to suspend flights left about 600 travelers stranded, mostly Argentine tourists, Viasa said.
"I've spent four extra days in Venezuela, how am I going to justify that to my boss?" asked one stranded passenger, worried that she might lose her job.

Other travelers were transferred free of charge to five-star hotels. "It's a delight ... we want to stay another week," Argentine tourist Belia Baudracco said on Margarita island, Venezuela's prime Caribbean tourist destination.
Viasa's difficulties worsened this month when workers overwhelmingly rejected an emergency cost-cutting plan, said to be the last attempt to save the partly Spanish-owned airline from bankruptcy.
Venezuela's National Investment Fund President Alberto Poletto, who is responsible for privatisations, met Spanish authorities in Madrid on Tuesday to try to save the airline.
State-owned Spanish carrier Iberia holds the largest stake in Viasa with 45 percent. Venezuela has a 40 percent share and Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial, owns 15 percent.
Viasa, which employs about 2,200 people and was founded 35 years ago, had a $30 million loss last year and has not reported a profit since Iberia took over management in 1991.
